The Big Story · Space

At 4:41 a.m., Japan began a five-year hunt for ten grams.

MMX rose from Tanegashima into a black sky this morning. If the mission succeeds, the dust it brings home from Phobos could settle whether Mars captured a wandering asteroid—or built a moon from an ancient collision.

Today in Japan

Culture · Noh · Tokyo

The star is not the whole stage.

At the National Noh Theatre today, young performers show how supporting actors, musicians and Kyogen specialists keep a 700-year-old form alive. The 41st Seishokai is less a museum display than a public step in a six-year training system.

Politics · Diet

A grocery tax cut enters debate. Restaurant meals stay outside.

Japan’s food-consumption-tax reduction bill enters Diet deliberation today. The proposal concerns food and drink purchases, while restaurant dining remains taxed at 10%. That boundary affects shops, delivery, takeout and restaurant accounting differently.

Lawmakers must address replacement revenue and implementation costs, while food-service businesses warn that a wider gap could change customer behavior. Today marks the start of deliberation, not enactment; current tax rates remain in force.

Science · What happens next

Launch was the visible minute. The difficult years are next.

MMX is designed to reach the Mars region in 2027, survey Phobos, deploy the French-German IDEFIX rover, attempt two surface operations, depart in 2030 and return a capsule to Australia in 2031. Every date after launch is a target, not a completed milestone.

CNES supplied the MIRS spectrometer and worked with DLR on IDEFIX; ESA is contributing communications support. Japan leads the mission, but the ten grams are the product of a multinational chain.

Culture · On today

Five short works expose Noh’s machinery

The Seishokai program begins at 1 p.m. in Sendagaya with four maibayashi excerpts—Takasago, Hashitomi, Kumasaka and Kakitsubata—plus the Kyogen comedy Fune Funa. A maibayashi removes full costume and mask so chant, dance and instrumental structure come forward.

The ¥1,300 performance is organized for training and skills development. Audiences are seeing younger artists in a professional learning process, not a claim of finished mastery.

Japanese word of the day打上げ · うちあげ · uchiage

Launch. 打 means “strike” and 上げ means “raise,” but in space reporting the compound refers to launching a rocket or spacecraft. Official agencies often write ロケットの打上げ; the verb is 打ち上げる.

The same sound can also mean a post-event party (打ち上げ), so context matters. MMX no uchiage wa gozen yoji yonjuippun deshita means “MMX’s launch was at 4:41 a.m.” Today’s article uses the technical news sense. Learn words in context with DraMap for iOS.
